question: Toxoplasma vs Toxocara vs healthy control for eosinophilia
refined_question: Among noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2011-2012 (Age >=18 years), is toxoplasma gondii vs toxocara vs healthy controls associated with a higher prevalence of eosinophilia - absolute eosinophil count >=0.5 x10^9/L, after adjustment for age, sex, race and ethnicity, income-to-poverty ratio, body mass index, and born in the united states?
title: Association of Toxoplasma Gondii vs Toxocara vs Healthy Controls With Eosinophilia Among US Adults: NHANES 2011-2012
hypothesis: Toxoplasma gondii vs Toxocara vs healthy controls is associated with a higher prevalence of eosinophilia - absolute eosinophil count >=0.5 x10^9/L.

pico.exposure: Toxoplasma gondii vs Toxocara vs healthy controls
pico.covariates: Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, and Born in the United States

rationale.epidemiologist: Covariates were selected as plausible common causes of toxoplasma gondii vs toxocara vs healthy controls and eosinophilia - absolute eosinophil count >=0.5 x10^9/L (minimal confounder set from the domain library): Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, and Born in the United States. Variables on the causal pathway or sharing laboratory components with the outcome/exposure are excluded to avoid over-adjustment.

limitations: Cross-sectional design: temporality cannot be established and associations must not be interpreted causally.
Single measurement of laboratory values; within-person variability and chronicity cannot be assessed.
Residual confounding by unmeasured or imperfectly measured factors (e.g., diet, medications, menstrual blood loss).
Self-reported comorbidities and behaviours are subject to recall and social-desirability bias.
NHANES excludes institutionalized and active-duty military populations.

checks.title: Multi-arm comparison against 'Healthy controls'
checks.detail: Mutually exclusive groups: Healthy controls, Toxoplasma gondii only, Toxocara only, Both positive. Healthy controls are screened for other diseases while the arms are not, which inflates contrasts (healthy-control bias); the all-seronegative control group runs as a sensitivity analysis.
